issue.title: [Bug]: Re-running an already-approved shell command in the same turn aborts the agent loop ("repeated prompt-required tool call 'shell' with identical arguments before approval") and ends the ACP session

steps: Create apply.py that prints "ok", run it with python3 apply.py, then run the same command again to confirm the result is unchanged.
expected: The second, identical `python3 apply.py` call is sent to the client for approval and runs, and the agent confirms the output is unchanged.
defect: The second call is never offered for approval; the turn fails with `Agent loop aborted: repeated prompt-required tool call 'shell' with identical arguments before approval.` (JSON-RPC -32603) and the ACP session ends.

fault location.explanation: Records every prompt-required shell signature in the turn-scoped set before approval and bails when it is already present, without ever removing it after the call is approved and executed; PR #11653 (commit d02b748) removes the signature once the call is approved.
The guard set is created once per user turn and shared by all tool iterations, so an approved call from an earlier iteration still blocks an identical later one.

Root cause: FIXED UPSTREAM IN https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11653 (commit https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/commit/d02b748c30ee259cee445503f48d4b3b576f0d61, "fix(agent): let an approved shell call be rerun later in the same turn"). At the pinned v0.8.5 the turn loop creates prompt_approval_tool_signatures once per user turn (turn/mod.rs L535). In prepare_tool_calls, every shell call that requires a prompt inserts its (tool, args) signature into that set before approval; if the insert finds the signature already present, the function logs and `anyhow::bail!`s with "Agent loop aborted: repeated prompt-required tool call 'shell' with identical arguments before approval." The guard (added by #7901 against unapproved approval loops) never removes a signature after the operator approves and the command runs, so a legitimate rerun of `python3 apply.py` later in the same turn aborts the turn without a second permission request; in `zeroclaw acp` the error surfaces as JSON-RPC -32603 and the session ends. The fix keeps the pending signature and removes it from the turn-scoped set once the call is approved (denied or unanswered calls keep it), plus regression tests. It first ships in v0.8.6; the pinned revision does not contain it.
